[[File:1924WOlympicPoster.jpg|thumb|right|Publicity poster for the event|alt=As caption]]
The [[1924 Winter Olympics]], officially known as the I Olympic Winter Games, and known at the time as ''Semaine Internationale des Sports d'Hiver'' ("International Winter Sports Week"), was a [[winter sport|winter]] [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Chamonix]], France, from 25 January to 5 February 1924. [[Norway at the 1924 Winter Olympics|Norway]] topped the table, collecting seventeen medals in total, including four gold,<ref name="table">{{cite web |url=http://www.topendsports.com/events/winter/medal-tally/1924.htm |title=1924 Medal Tally |website=Topend Sports |access-date=25 August 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825150306/http://www.topendsports.com/events/winter/medal-tally/1924.htm |archive-date=25 August 2017 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> three of which were won by [[Thorleif Haug]] in the [[Nordic combined at the 1924 Winter Olympics|Nordic combined]] and [[Cross-country skiing at the 1924 Winter Olympics|cross-country skiing]] events.<ref name="ioc1924">{{cite web |url=https://www.olympic.org/chamonix-1924 |title=Chamonix 1924 |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=24 August 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170901162819/https://www.olympic.org/chamonix-1924 |archive-date=1 September 2017 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> Norway also achieved two podium sweeps, winning all three medals in both the [[Cross-country skiing at the 1924 Winter Olympics – Men's 50 km|50 km cross-country skiing]] and the Nordic combined. This remained a record at the Winter Olympics until [[2014 Winter Olympics|2014]].{{efn|No country achieved more than two podium sweeps until the Netherlands in [[List of 2014 Winter Olympics medal winners|2014]], but the record was tied prior to that; by Norway themselves in [[List of 1928 Winter Olympics medal winners|1928]] and [[List of 1932 Winter Olympics medal winners|1932]], the Soviet Union in [[List of 1964 Winter Olympics medal winners|1964]], East Germany in [[List of 1928 Winter Olympics medal winners|1972]] and [[List of 1984 Winter Olympics medal winners|1984]], and Germany in [[List of 1998 Winter Olympics medal winners|1998]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://olympstats.com/2014/02/18/netherlands-speed-skating-medal-sweeps/ |title=Netherlands Speed Skating Medal Sweeps |website=OlympStats |author=BMallon |date=18 February 2014 |access-date=25 August 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825152012/http://olympstats.com/2014/02/18/netherlands-speed-skating-medal-sweeps/ |archive-date=25 August 2017 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>}}<ref>{{cite news |url=http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/sports/2014-02/19/c_133125438.htm |title=Bergsma breaks Olympic record to lead fourth Dutch medal sweep |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923061814/http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/sports/2014-02/19/c_133125438.htm |archive-date=23 September 2015 |website=[[Xinhua News Agency|Xinhuanet]] |date=19 February 2014 |access-date=25 August 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

When it was held, the games were not formally recognised as being the Olympics, but acknowledged that they were held under the "high patronage of the International Olympic Committee".<ref name="sr1924">{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/1924/ |title=1924 Chamonix Winter Games |website=[[Sports Reference]] |access-date=25 August 2017 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825151216/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/1924/ |archive-date=25 August 2017 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> Partly due to this, varying figures are reported for the number of participants. The [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) website suggests that 258 athletes from 16 nations participated in 16 events across 9 sports.<ref name="ioc1924"/> In contrast, the ''[[Sports Reference|Sports-Reference]]'' website lists 313 participants from 19 countries.<ref name="sr1924"/> [[Bill Mallon]], a prominent Olympic Games historian, quotes a figure of 291 competitors in his ''Historical Dictionary of the Olympic Movement''.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9mM0XzW03AcC&pg=PR46 |title=Historical Dictionary of the Olympic Movement |last1=Mallon |first1=Bill |author1-link=Bill Mallon |last2=Heijmans |first2=Jereon |year=2011 |publisher=[[Scarecrow Press]] |location=Plymouth, UK |isbn=978-0-8108-7522-7 |page=46 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171014183319/https://books.google.co.uk/books?id=9mM0XzW03AcC&pg=PR46 |archive-date=14 October 2017 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> Meanwhile, the official report for the 1924 Summer and Winter Olympics listed 293 athletes from 17 nations.<ref>{{cite book |url=http://library.la84.org/6oic/OfficialReports/1924/1924.pdf |title="Official Report of the 1924 Olympic Games |year=1924 |publisher=International Olympic Committee |language=fr |page=[http://library.la84.org/6oic/OfficialReports/1924/1924.pdf#page=660 662] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160226232716/http://library.la84.org/6oic/OfficialReports/1924/1924.pdf |archive-date=26 February 2016 |df=dmy-all |access-date=14 October 2017 }}</ref>

[[Finland at the 1924 Winter Olympics|Finland]] placed second on the table, collecting four gold medals amongst a total of eleven. [[Clas Thunberg]] won five of their medals, achieving a medal in each of the [[Speed skating at the 1924 Winter Olympics|speed skating]] events he took part in; collecting three gold medals, one silver and one bronze.<ref name="ioc1924"/> Eight of the competing nations achieved at least one gold medal, with only [[Belgium at the 1924 Winter Olympics|Belgium]] and the hosts, [[France at the 1924 Winter Olympics|France]], medalling without winning a gold medal.<ref name="table"/> One medal was reallocated in 1974; during the games, Thorleif Haug of Norway had been awarded the bronze medal in [[Ski jumping at the 1924 Winter Olympics|ski jumping]], along with his three gold medals. A Norwegian historian discovered that there had been a scoring error, and an [[United States at the 1924 Winter Olympics|American]], [[Anders Haugen]], had actually finished in third place. As Haug had died in 1934, his daughter presented Haugen, aged 83, with his medal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://nbl.snl.no/Thorleif_Haug |title=Thorleif Haug |website=[[Norsk biografisk leksikon]] |language=no |location=Oslo |publisher=[[Kunnskapsforlaget]] |last=Jorsett |first=Per |date=13 February 2009 |access-date=20 September 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170921000336/https://nbl.snl.no/Thorleif_Haug |archive-date=21 September 2017 |df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.skisprungschanzen.com/EN/Articles/28-Anders+Haugen%E2%80%99s+belated+bronze+medal/ |title=Anders Haugen's belated bronze medal |website=Ski Jumping Hill Archive |date=5 January 2006 |access-date=20 September 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170921000414/http://www.skisprungschanzen.com/EN/Articles/28-Anders+Haugen%E2%80%99s+belated+bronze+medal/ |archive-date=21 September 2017 |df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1984/04/19/obituaries/anders-haugen-olympian-medal-was-delayed-50-years.html?mcubz=1 |title=Anders Haugen, Olympian; Medal Was Delayed 50 Years |work=[[The New York Times]] |agency=[[Associated Press|AP]] |date=19 April 1984 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170920191141/http://www.nytimes.com/1984/04/19/obituaries/anders-haugen-olympian-medal-was-delayed-50-years.html?mcubz=1 |archive-date=20 September 2017 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

In the official report, the classification of nations is ranked not by medals, but rather by "points", which were awarded for each position from first to sixth; not exclusively for gold, silver and bronze. Due to this, [[Czechoslovakia at the 1924 Winter Olympics|Czechoslovakia]] were included in the table ahead of Belgium, due to two fourth-place finishes, one fifth and one sixth. [[Italy at the 1924 Winter Olympics|Italy]] were also present, in twelfth, for their solitary sixth place.<ref>{{cite book |url=http://library.la84.org/6oic/OfficialReports/1924/1924.pdf |title="Official Report of the 1924 Olympic Games |year=1924 |publisher=International Olympic Committee |language=fr |page=[http://library.la84.org/6oic/OfficialReports/1924/1924.pdf#page=659 661] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160226232716/http://library.la84.org/6oic/OfficialReports/1924/1924.pdf |archive-date=26 February 2016 |df=dmy-all |access-date=14 October 2017 }}</ref>

==Medal table==
[[File:Clas Thunberg signed.jpg|thumb|right|[[Clas Thunberg]] won five [[Speed skating at the 1924 Winter Olympics|speed skating]] medals at the games for [[Finland at the 1924 Winter Olympics|Finland]].<ref name="ioc1924"/>|alt=A signed black and white photograph of Clas Thunberg skating]]
The medal table is based on information provided by the IOC and is consistent with IOC convention in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a [[National Olympic Committee]] (NOC). The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next, and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |date=11 August 2024 |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |access-date=12 August 2024 |work=[[The Independent]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |date=18 August 2008 |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |access-date=25 July 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |date=10 August 2024 |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=August 11, 2024 |access-date=11 August 2024 |work=[[Diario AS]] |language=en-us}}</ref> Two bronze medals were awarded in the [[Speed skating at the 1924 Winter Olympics – Men's 500 metres|500 metres speed skating]] event for the third place tie.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympic.org/chamonix-1924/speed-skating/500m-men |title=Chamonix 1924 / Speed Skating / 500m Men |publisher=International Olympic Committee |access-date=25 August 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170327033846/https://www.olympic.org/chamonix-1924/speed-skating/500m-men |archive-date=27 March 2017 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

[[Pierre de Coubertin]]—founder of the [[IOC]] & father of the modern Olympics movement—personally awarded, in addition to the medals awarded in the sports competitions, 21 gold medals to members of the [[1922 British Mount Everest Expedition]] including 12 Britons, 7 Indians, 1 Australian and 1 Nepalese.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-17493939 |date=26 March 2012 |title=Everest Olympic medal pledge set to be honoured |first=Mark |last=Georgiou |access-date=31 August 2012 |work=BBC News |archive-date=22 September 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140922145422/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-17493939 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/may/19/olympic-secret-everest-forgotten-hero |title=My modest father never mentioned his Everest expedition Olympic gold |first=Ed |last=Douglas |work=The Guardian |date=19 May 2012 |access-date=31 August 2012 |location=London |archive-date=25 December 2018 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20181225173145/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/may/19/olympic-secret-everest-forgotten-hero |url-status=live }}</ref> Only the gold medal from 1924 is assigned to the [[Winter Olympics]] by the IOC in its database to the [[Mixed teams at the Olympics|Mixed team]],<ref name="Olympedia">{{cite web | title=Olympedia – Alpinism | website=Olympedia – Main Page | url=https://www.olympedia.org/sports/APN | access-date=2024-01-28}}</ref><ref name="1924_olympics.com">{{cite web | url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/chamonix-1924/medals | title=Chamonix 1924 Olympic Medal Table | website=olympics.com| publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) |access-date=2024-08-15}}</ref> while the medals from 1932 and 1936 are assigned to the [[Summer Olympics]] for the respective NOCs.<ref name="GER_profile">{{cite web | url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/germany | title=Germany - NOC Profile | website=olympics.com| publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) | date=2024 |access-date=2024-08-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240815122428/http://web.archive.org/screenshot/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/germany |archive-date=15 August 2024 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="SUI_profile">{{cite web | url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/switzerland | title=Switzerland - NOC Profile | website=olympics.com| publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) | date=2024 |access-date=2024-08-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240815122855/http://web.archive.org/screenshot/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/switzerland |archive-date=15 August 2024 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
